rationale: Frameshift predicted to disrupt a microtubule-binding protein; loss of microtubule/mitotic spindle function in AMso would directly impair the asymmetric division that generates MCM neurons. [Effect=frameshift_variant; impact_bucket=HIGH; EMS_label=non-EMS]
Narrative: A frameshift (HIGH-impact) in Y55F3C.17 is predicted to abolish normal microtubule-binding/cytoskeletal function. Proper spindle assembly and microtubule dynamics are essential for asymmetric mitoses that produce a neuron versus a glial daughter; loss of this function in AMso would plausibly cause the observed failure of the neurogenic division and loss of MCM neurons. [Effect=frameshift_variant; impact_bucket=HIGH; EMS_label=non-EMS]

rationale: CDK-4 is a core G1/S cell-cycle kinase; a damaging missense could perturb cell-cycle progression or timing in AMso, preventing the timely asymmetric division required to produce an MCM neuron. Disruption of CDK function is a plausible mechanistic cause of division/fate defects during male maturation. [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE]
Narrative: CDK-4 is a cell-cycle kinase that promotes G1/S progression and is involved in cell-cycle regulation in many tissues. A missense (MODERATE-impact) could alter CDK-4 activity or regulation in AMso, preventing the cell-cycle change required for the asymmetric, neuron-generating division during male maturation, thereby eliminating MCMs. [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE]

rationale: Stop_gained (HIGH) likely causes loss-of-function of a cytochrome P450. Although P450s are metabolic enzymes, some cytochrome products control developmental or hormonal signals that trigger sexually dimorphic maturation; impaired maturation signaling could explain failure of AMso to execute its neurogenic division. This is indirect but the high-impact nature of the lesion gives some prior. [Effect=stop_gained; impact_bucket=HIGH; EMS_label=non-EMS]
Narrative: This stop_gained (HIGH-impact) mutation likely causes loss-of-function of a cytochrome P450. While P450s often act in metabolism, some are required for producing hormones or small molecules that control developmental timing and sexual maturation; disruption could indirectly prevent AMso from executing the male-specific neurogenic division. This is a plausible but indirect mechanism. [Effect=stop_gained; impact_bucket=HIGH; EMS_label=non-EMS]

rationale: NFKI-1 is related to NF-κB inhibitor family and is predicted to regulate transcription and positive regulation of cell differentiation; a missense could alter transcriptional programs needed for AMso-to-MCM neurogenic fate. The gene is expressed in nervous system tissues, increasing plausibility. [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 28099418]
Narrative: NFKI-1 is predicted to regulate transcription and positively regulate cell differentiation, and it is expressed in nervous system tissues. A missense (MODERATE-impact) could impair transcriptional control of genes required for AMso-to-MCM fate transition, offering a mechanistic route to MCM loss. [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 28099418]

rationale: CLA-1 encodes an active-zone presynaptic protein; a missense could perturb neuronal connectivity or maturation rather than the glial asymmetric division itself. Because the phenotype is absence of MCM neuronal differentiation, CLA-1 is a less direct candidate but nervous-system expression gives minor plausibility. [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 29160205, 37186867, 39708832]
Narrative: CLA-1 encodes an active-zone presynaptic protein required for synaptic function; a missense (MODERATE-impact) is more likely to affect synaptic maturation than the glial asymmetric division itself. While synaptic defects could secondarily affect neuronal maintenance, CLA-1 is a less direct candidate for elimination of MCM neuron birth. [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 29160205, 37186867, 39708832]

rationale: PKS-1 is a polyketide synthase; metabolic products could conceivably act as developmental signals during sexual maturation. [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 34389721, 38915494, 39103170]

[Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 34389721, 38915494, 39103170]

[Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; GeneRef: PMID 35800971]
